chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: He told me Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Hamiri, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Any Muslim servant whom God advises sincerely regarding his own soul, giving it its due right and taking its due right for it, is granted two characteristics: sustenance from God, the Exalted and Mighty, with which he is content, and God's Pleasure with which he is saved.

key_terms.نَاصَحَ: To advise sincerely or give due rights

ai.seo_question: What are the two characteristics granted to a believer who sincerely advises their own soul?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that sincere self-advice (nasihah) involves balancing the soul's rights and duties, a concept central to Shia spiritual psychology. The promised rewards—sustenance that brings contentment (qana'ah) and divine pleasure (rida)—are not merely material but serve as the ultimate means of salvation (najah) from divine reckoning.
